top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B001) rewards one identifiable idea: firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment, with reallocation across firms as a channel for the gains from trade. It rests on Melitz (2003) and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple (2004), which have been tested and extended in firm-level data for more than twenty years. Its attribution to two names is defensible if the citation stays on selection and reallocation, makes no claim about welfare magnitudes, and leaves the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum empirical lineage and Redding's quantitative-trade work to the scientific background. The residual risk is that the Committee defines the discovery more broadly, which would make a two-name award too narrow. That risk, and the alternatives (B006 as a fallback if a clean Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes boundary can be drawn), do not outweigh the case for a mature, well-bounded achievement over no award. The unanimity in the round-2 files is not evidence of merit, so this ranking rests on the content of the discovery, not the vote count.
